The settings reference documents every key, including the managed-only ones: <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings">code.claude.com/docs/en/settings</a></div></div></div></div><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">How to measure it (for the hooks themselves)</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Leading indicator</b><div>Time spent waiting on each approval gate. Every hook decision is written to the OpenTelemetry export with a timestamp and an allow or block verdict, so the wait is visible per gate.</div></div><div><b>Lagging indicator</b><div>Gate violations reaching production before and after hooks from the incident tracker.</div></div></div></div><h3>CI/CD integration and deployment</h3><p>Run Claude Code non-interactively inside the CI/CD pipeline, sandbox the execution so long-running agents run safely, expose deployment through MCP integrations, and rehearse the rollback paths before the agent ever needs them.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-vs"><div class="sd-old"><small>Traditional</small>Pipelines run deterministic scripts, and anything that needs judgment waits for a human. For example, triaging the flaky test, writing the changelog, or working out why the build broke. Deployment and rollback are runbooks a human follows under pressure.</div><div class="sd-new"><small>AI-native</small>Claude runs non-interactively inside the pipeline for the judgment steps, in a sandbox with scoped credentials. Deployment tooling is exposed to the agent through MCP, so the workflow that wrote and tested the change can also ship it and roll it back, inside gates the organization defines per environment.</div></div></div><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">Getting started</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Prerequisites</b><div>Claude in the PR review loop and hooks as approval gates, because the gates must exist before automation accelerates anything through them.</div></div><div><b>Infrastructure</b><div>A CI platform with the claude-code-action installed, or any runner that can call <code>claude -p</code>; model access through the API, or Bedrock, Foundry, or Vertex where traffic must stay on the organization's cloud agreement; MCP servers for the deployment targets; a sandbox profile for agent jobs with no standing production credentials.</div></div></div></div><h4>How to execute it</h4><ol><li>The platform engineer starts with read-only judgment steps. Use <code>claude -p</code> in a pipeline job to triage a failed build, summarize a flaky test, or draft the changelog.</li><li>Add write steps behind the existing gates for jobs like fixing lint, updating generated docs, or addressing review comments via the <code>@claude</code> mentions. Anything the agent writes arrives as a PR through branch protection, and the agent has no route to push to main.</li><li>Execution is sandboxed. Agent jobs run in containers under a network policy with short-lived scoped tokens, and hold no production credentials by default.</li><li>Expose deployment through MCP. Deploy, status, and rollback become tools, scoped per environment, so the agent&#x27;s deployment powers are an allowlist rather than a shell script with credentials.</li><li>Tier the autonomy by environment. In development, the agent deploys freely. In production, the agent prepares the release and the release manager authorizes it, and a hook enforces the production gate. Staging sits somewhere in the middle.</li><li>Rollback should be the most rehearsed path in the pipeline, a single command that the agent can run and that is exercised regularly in staging. The closing the loop play (Stage 6: Maintenance) calls this rollback when a control band is breached, so it has to be proven in advance.</li></ol><h4>What it looks like (pipeline step)</h4><div class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__block" data-cta-ignore=""><button class="Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__button Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__variant-secondary Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__size-small Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__hasTrailingIcon text-caption CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__copy" aria-label="Copy code">Copy<span class="Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__icon"><div class="_base-module-scss-module__SsgDWW__wrapper" style="width:16px;height:16px"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="_base-module-scss-module__SsgDWW__vector" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z"></path></svg></div></span></button><pre class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__pre"><code class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__code language-markdown">- name: Triage failed build
  if: failure()
  run: &gt;
    claude -p &quot;Read the build log at out/build.log. Identify the most
    likely cause, say whether the failure looks flaky or real, and write a
    three-line summary for the PR thread.&quot; &gt;&gt; triage.md</code></pre></div><h4>Governance considerations</h4><p>The governing principle is that the agent may act up to the production gate and cannot pass it. The controls below enforce this principle.</p><ul><li>Branch protection turns anything the agent writes into a PR, with no direct path to main.</li><li>The production deploy hook blocks the release until a named release manager authorizes it. Each non-interactive run acts under the agent&#x27;s own identity, so the pipeline log separates what the agent did from what the engineer who triggered it did.</li><li>Per-environment permission tiers set how much the agent may do on the way to the gate.</li></ul><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">How to measure it</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Leading indicator</b><div>The share of pipeline failures triaged without paging a human taken from the CI/CD pipeline logs.</div></div><div><b>Lagging indicator</b><div>DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) measures, which the CI system and deployment tooling already emit.</div></div></div></div><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-band" id="sd-s6" style="background:#ece7da"><b>06</b><div><h2>Maintain</h2><div>The loop closes. A trigger invokes Claude with no person in the invocation path, and what it finds re-enters the pipeline as <code style="font-family:Menlo,Consolas,monospace;font-size:.88em;background:rgba(20,20,19,.07);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px">intent.md</code>.</div></div></div></div><h3>Maintenance and closing the loop</h3><p>So far, we&#x27;ve discussed how to add Claude to each stage of the SDLC process, with each stage requiring a human to launch the initial steps. This stage, however, shifts the focus to autonomous running of Claude to close the loop.</p><p>For example, a continuously running monitoring agent could, off the back of a bug ticket being raised, create an <code>intent.md</code>, and flow through the requirements, plan, build test and review phases. Stage 6: Maintenance runs headless, with an independent confidence gate between stages, a deterministic check or an adversarial reviewing agent, deciding whether the previous stage&#x27;s output continues or is escalated to a human.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-vs"><div class="sd-old"><small>Traditional</small>Maintenance is a reactive phase. All tickets or incidents wait on a person to act on it and restart the process. An alert fires at 3 a.m. and can be missed, a ticket can sit in the backlog until someone picks it up, and post-mortem actions may not reach the codebase at all if another fire starts first.</div><div class="sd-new"><small>AI-native</small>A trigger such as a control-band breach, a ticket, a channel message or a schedule invokes Claude without a person in the path. Claude diagnoses, acts only through gated routes, and writes what it finds as <code>intent.md</code>, which then goes through the stages described above. People triage and review that work, and no longer have to start it.</div></div></div><h3>Closing the loop</h3><p>A deterministic script watches production and invokes Claude when a control band is breached. Monitoring of a breach is a helpful example of the pattern for the loop running autonomously, while the <a href="https://claude.com/product/tag">Claude Tag</a> (public beta) section at the end of the stage covers work arriving through different channels.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">Getting started</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Prerequisites</b><div><code>Intent.md</code> which gives the loop a structured output to restart. Claude accelerated PR reviews, hooks as an action boundary, and a rollback path for CI/CD (which the highest autonomy tier invokes).</div></div><div><b>Infrastructure</b><div>A metrics store the detection script can query (Prometheus, the CI system's API, or equivalents), read access to the repository, a way to run Claude Code non-interactively in CI, or the <a href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview">Agent SDK</a> for a service that receives webhooks.</div></div></div></div><h4>How to execute it</h4><ol><li>The service owner or platform engineer picks one metric with a stable rolling baseline, such as CI test failure rate, post-deploy 5xx rate, or PR cycle time.</li><li>They write the detection script, typically mean and standard deviation over a rolling window with rules (Western Electric or similar) so the bands catch slow drift as well as spikes. The script is version controlled and unit tested, and detection stays entirely deterministic, with no model involved.</li><li>Response tiers are defined in version-controlled config (<code>bands.yaml</code> below). At 1σ the script only logs, at 2σ it invokes Claude read-only to diagnose, and at 3σ Claude may act, though only by opening a PR into the review gate or triggering a pre-approved runbook.</li><li>The trigger layer can be a scheduled workflow in GitHub or GitLab, a webhook from the existing monitoring stack, or a Cron Job inside the network. Claude runs stateless, either as a non-interactive step on a CI runner or as an Agent SDK service in a sandboxed container, and the CI/CD play covers the deployment and model-access options. Because the run is stateless and non-interactive, a loop can begin and end without anyone starting it.</li><li>The agent writes its diagnosis as <code>intent.md</code> in the Stage 1: Plan format, covering the anomaly and its evidence, a proposed outcome, the affected systems and any open questions. From there the finding goes through the pipeline like anything else.</li><li>The service owner or on-call engineer triages the queue, routing product-facing findings to the product owner. Fix now, schedule, or dismiss. Dismissals tune the bands and help to reduce noise.</li><li>When a fix ships, add an eval for the incident (the continuous evals play) to ensure that such issues are protected against going forwards.</li></ol><h4>What it looks like (for example, a bands.yaml monitoring CI test failure rate)</h4><div class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__block" data-cta-ignore=""><button class="Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__button Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__variant-secondary Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__size-small Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__hasTrailingIcon text-caption CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__copy" aria-label="Copy code">Copy<span class="Button-module-scss-module__1SItCG__icon"><div class="_base-module-scss-module__SsgDWW__wrapper" style="width:16px;height:16px"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="_base-module-scss-module__SsgDWW__vector" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.5 3C13.3284 3 14 3.67157 14 4.5V6H15.5C16.3284 6 17 6.67157 17 7.5V15.5C17 16.3284 16.3284 17 15.5 17H7.5C6.67157 17 6 16.3284 6 15.5V14H4.5C3.67157 14 3 13.3284 3 12.5V4.5C3 3.67157 3.67157 3 4.5 3H12.5ZM14 12.5C14 13.3284 13.3284 14 12.5 14H7V15.5C7 15.7761 7.22386 16 7.5 16H15.5C15.7761 16 16 15.7761 16 15.5V7.5C16 7.22386 15.7761 7 15.5 7H14V12.5ZM4.5 4C4.22386 4 4 4.22386 4 4.5V12.5C4 12.7761 4.22386 13 4.5 13H12.5C12.7761 13 13 12.7761 13 12.5V4.5C13 4.22386 12.7761 4 12.5 4H4.5Z"></path></svg></div></span></button><pre class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__pre"><code class="CodeBlock-module-scss-module__aqLerq__code language-yaml">metric: ci_test_failure_rate
baseline: rolling_30d
rules: western_electric
tiers:
  1sigma: { action: log }
  2sigma: { action: diagnose,
            tools: &quot;Read,Grep,Bash(gh run view *)&quot; }
  3sigma: { action: propose,
            routes: [pull_request, runbook:rollback-deploy] }</code></pre></div><h4>Governance considerations</h4><p>The tier boundaries are enforced from version-controlled config, with permissions and managed settings denying production access. Invocations, findings and triage decisions are logged with a timestamp. A service owner triages and approves findings, resulting changes go through the normal PR review gate, and the runbooks the agent may trigger were approved in advance.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">How to measure it</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Leading indicator</b><div>Time from band breach to an <code>intent.md</code> in the triage queue, against the old time from incident to post-mortem action. The detection script's log has the breach timestamp and tier of incident.</div></div><div><b>Lagging indicator</b><div>The share of findings that become merged fixes (triage queue against actual PR history), and repeat incidents of the same class, which should fall as the fixes add cases to the eval suite.</div></div></div></div><h4>Examples</h4><ul><li>When the CI test failure rate breaches 3σ, the agent quarantines the flaky test or opens a revert PR, and the review gate decides.</li><li>When the post-deploy 5xx rate breaches 3σ with a deployment in the window, the agent triggers the existing rollback pipeline.</li><li>When PR cycle time trips a drift rule, the agent writes a report for engineering leadership, which shows the harness works for process metrics as well as production ones.</li></ul><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-key" style="background:#ece7da"><svg viewBox="0 0 44 44" fill="none" stroke="#141413" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M4 24h8l4-12 6 22 5-16 3 6h10"></path></svg><div>Detection stays deterministic. Claude is invoked once a band is breached, and the tier sets what it may do.</div></div></div><h3>Recurring codebase scans</h3><p>A security scan is a point-in-time statement about a codebase under a particular model, and both halves go stale: the code changes every week, and each model generation finds vulnerabilities the previous one missed. The AI-native answer is to run the scan on a schedule, without a human in the invocation path, and to send what it finds through the same gates as any other change to the codebase.</p><p><a href="https://claude.com/product/claude-security">Claude Security</a> is the hosted form of scheduled scanning. Connect a GitHub repository, and scans run on Claude Mythos 5 in Anthropic&#x27;s infrastructure, with each finding validated before it is reported and a confidence rating attached. Suggested patches are reviewed and applied in Claude Code on the web. The organization gets the findings without needing access to the model itself.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-vs"><div class="sd-old"><small>Traditional</small>Security scanning is an event with a scan launched before a release or an audit. The report goes to a tracker, and the backlog is worked down by hand until the next event. Code written in between is covered by whatever the PR review caught.</div><div class="sd-new"><small>AI-native</small>Scans run on a schedule against every connected repository, on the most capable model available, with findings validated before anyone reads them. Each finding is handled the way a breached control band is: a fix that fits in one PR goes through the review gate, and anything larger becomes an <code>intent.md</code>. Coverage is dated from the last run, not from the first</div></div></div><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">Getting started</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Prerequisites</b><div>The PR review gate and hooks as approval gates (<a href="#sd-s5">Stage 5: Deploy</a>), so that findings go through review like any other change. The <code>intent.md</code> format from <a href="#sd-s1">Stage 1: Plan</a> for findings too large for a single PR.</div></div><div><b>Infrastructure</b><div>Claude Security is available to Claude Enterprise organizations in public beta. It needs the Anthropic GitHub App installed on the target repositories (cloud-hosted github.com), Claude Code on the Web enabled, Extra Usage turned on with a spend limit set, premium seats for the people who run scans, and the feature switched on by an admin at <code>claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code</code>. Scans are billed on consumption at Mythos 5 rates, so the spend limit should match the size and number of repositories.</div></div></div></div><h4>How to execute it</h4><ol><li>The security lead connects the repositories and organizes them into projects by repo, service, or team, so ownership of findings is clear from the start.</li><li>Run a first full scan of the most critical repositories, including ones that have been scanned before by other tools or by earlier models. Treat the first scan as the baseline. The first scan will likely surface findings in code that was considered clean.</li><li>Set a schedule per project. Weekly is a sensible default for actively developed services; scope scans to a directory or branch where a repository is large or mixed.</li><li>Triage findings with the confidence rating in hand. Dismiss with a reason, so the dismissal is recorded and the same finding does not return as new on the next run.</li><li>For a bounded finding, open the suggested patch in Claude Code on the Web, review it, and send it through the PR review gate like any other change. The agent that proposed the fix has no route to approve it.</li><li>For anything wider than one patch, such as an architectural weakness or a pattern repeated across services, write it up as <code>intent.md</code> in the Stage 1 format and start it at Plan.</li><li>When a fix is released to production, add an eval for the vulnerability class to the suite from the continuous evals play, so the configuration that steers the agent is tested against that class from then on.</li><li>Export findings as CSV or Markdown, or use webhooks, to keep the organization&#x27;s existing tracker and audit systems as the system of record where auditors already expect them.</li></ol><h4>Governance considerations</h4><p>The scan runs under the organization&#x27;s admin controls meaning what repositories are connected, who holds a scan seat, and the spend limit are all set centrally. Every finding has a validation result and a confidence rating, and every dismissal has a reason, so the scan history is an audit record of what was found, fixed, and consciously accepted.</p><p>Fixes reach production through the PR review gate and branch protection rather than from the scan itself. Claude Security augments existing static analysis and dependency scanning. The deterministic checks stay in CI, and the model-driven scan covers the context-dependent vulnerabilities those checks are not built to find.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-k">How to measure it</div><div class="sd-kv"><div><b>Leading indicator</b><div>Share of connected repositories on a schedule, and time from a finding being reported to its patch entering the PR review gate, read from the scan history and the PR metadata.</div></div><div><b>Lagging indicator</b><div>Vulnerabilities found by the scheduled scan set against those found in production or by external report, from the incident tracker; and the trend in findings per scan on repositories that have been through several runs, which should fall as fixes and evals accumulate.</div></div></div></div><h3>Claude on call with Claude Tag</h3><p>Incidents can also arrive via other means such as workplace communication apps, like Slack or Teams. Incidents can look like a 10pm Slack message for an urgent fix on an incident channel and can now be actioned immediately. Claude Tag (public beta currently available in Slack) makes Claude a member of those channels under its own identity, so each new incident gets a first responder and the response itself becomes part of the loop and memory for future incidents.</p><p>The conversation and institutional knowledge stay in the channel, with anyone in the channel able to guide and action the response. Any team member can test hypotheses, explore new options and investigate in real time with the channel history adding to the auditability. Through access to MCP Claude verifies the metric is back at baseline and confirms it in the thread, writes the post-mortem to a version-controlled lessons file that future investigations can read.</p><p>Incidents are not the only work Claude Tag picks up. Tagged on a ticket over MCP or asked in the channel, Claude triages the work the same way. A small, well-bounded fix arrives as a PR through the review gate, and anything larger is written up as <code>intent.md</code> for Stage 1: Plan, at which point the loop starts feeding itself. See: <a href="https://claude.com/resources/articles/ai-ci-cd-on-call">how Claude Tag runs on-call for CI/CD at Anthropic</a>.</p><figure style="--media-natural-width:1400px"><img referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://assets.claude.com/c84d83832da7d5dcc41d79cd919446480f7755a7.png" width="1400" height="637" alt="" loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="Media-module-scss-module__7ZZCyW__image"/><figcaption>The channel is the audit trail: request, diagnosis, human authorization and fix all stay where the incident was handled.</figcaption></figure><h2 id="closing-thoughts">Closing thoughts</h2><p>Models and harnesses have become more advanced, allowing organizations to not just transform how they produce code, but the entire software development lifecycle.</p><p>This transformation keeps human judgement central to the process and considers the governance and regulation requirements of large enterprise organizations.</p><p>This guide consolidated many of the real best practices our Applied AI team executes on a daily basis for our customers, and we hope you found it a practical and actionable resource.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-close" id="sd-c9">The loop keeps running. Human judgement stays above it.</div></div><h3>Resources and acknowledgments</h3><p>The documentation below is what a platform team needs to set those controls up, in roughly the order you would roll them out.</p><div class="HtmlEmbed-module-scss-module__yZf7SG__embed" data-html-embed=""><div class="sd-res"><a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup">Set up Claude Code for your
